dialogue.content: Hey, I want to make sure you have some details about the people I work with on the product integration team. David Keane is a Senior Technical Lead on the product integration team. I started working with him on March 4th when I got moved over to this team. I keep second-guessing the order of words in his title, but it's definitely Senior Technical Lead.

Got it — David Keane, Senior Technical Lead on the product integration team, and you've been working with him since March 4th. I'll keep that title order straight for you: Senior first, then Technical Lead. If you need to reference him in emails or documents, I can help you draft those with the correct title. Do you have other colleagues on the team you'd like me to note as well?

Yes, actually. There's Priya Mukherjee — she's a Systems Analyst II on the same team. She was the person who walked me through the onboarding docs for the integration platform. I really enjoyed working with her because she explains things without burying you in jargon. She just gets straight to the point, which I appreciate a lot.

Noted — Priya Mukherjee, Systems Analyst II, and she handled your onboarding for the integration platform. It sounds like her communication style really clicked with yours. I'll remember that she's someone who keeps things clear and direct. If you ever need me to format onboarding notes or reference her contributions, I can pull that together quickly. Anyone else on the team I should know about, or any reporting relationships worth tracking?

Good question on reporting relationships. Tom Aldridge is the VP of Engineering now, he got promoted from Director of Engineering. He's David's manager. I sometimes mix up Tom and David's titles in my head, so having you remember this helps. Tom Aldridge, VP of Engineering, manages David Keane, Senior Technical Lead.

That's a helpful chain to keep straight. So the reporting line goes: Tom Aldridge, VP of Engineering, manages David Keane, Senior Technical Lead, who works on the product integration team with you. I can see how those titles might blur together since they're both senior leadership roles. Whenever you're drafting communications, I'll make sure Tom gets the VP title and David gets Senior Technical Lead. Is there anything else about the team structure you want me to hold onto?

One more person — Rachel Simmons just joined as a Junior Developer. I haven't worked with her much yet. My friend Marcus on the design team mentioned she came from an internship at the same company, so she's still pretty new to full-time work. That's the core team for now. I'll update you if anything changes.

Perfect, I've got the full picture now. Rachel Simmons, Junior Developer, recently joined from an internal internship, and your friend Marcus on the design team gave you that background. So the key people are: David Keane (Senior Technical Lead), Priya Mukherjee (Systems Analyst II), Tom Aldridge (VP of Engineering, David's manager), and Rachel Simmons (Junior Developer). I'll keep all of this organized and ready whenever you need to reference anyone for emails, meeting notes, or org charts.

Quick update on David. David's now acting as interim team lead for our sub-group on top of his Senior Technical Lead role. Someone left the team and they haven't found a permanent replacement, so David's wearing two hats for now. I'm not sure how long this arrangement will last, but it's the current situation as of this week.

Thanks for the update. So David Keane is now carrying both his Senior Technical Lead responsibilities and an interim team lead role for your sub-group while they search for a permanent replacement. That's a significant workload increase for him. I'll track his current role as Senior Technical Lead plus Interim Team Lead. If you need to reference his capacity or responsibilities in any communications, I can help frame that accurately. Do you know if this changes anything about your reporting line?

Not really — Tom Aldridge is still the VP overseeing everything. David's just handling the day-to-day coordination for our sub-group now. One thing I've noticed is that David still keeps his one-on-ones really efficient. Fifteen minutes, written agenda beforehand, no small talk. I genuinely enjoy that format. I'd rather have a short focused meeting than an hour of meandering conversation.

That's a great sign that even with the extra responsibility, David's maintaining his efficient meeting style. Fifteen-minute one-on-ones with a pre-written agenda is pretty disciplined — it shows he values everyone's time even under increased pressure. And it aligns well with your preference for direct, focused communication. If you ever want me to help you prepare agenda items or talking points for those quick check-ins with David, I'm happy to help. Is there anything else shifting on the team?

Yeah, unfortunately Priya got moved to a different project under a new manager. That happened around April 11th. I was honestly pretty bummed about it because we'd built up a solid working rhythm. The few days after that I was in a noticeably worse mood at work, just dreading having to establish all that context with someone new on the integration platform.

I'm sorry to hear that — losing a good working relationship like that is genuinely frustrating, especially when you'd found someone whose communication style matched yours so well. April 11th for the transition is noted. It makes sense that you'd feel low about having to rebuild that rapport and context from scratch. If it helps, I can compile the key onboarding details and integration platform notes that Priya walked you through, so you have a reference document ready for whoever steps into her role on your team.

That's a good idea, actually. I might take you up on that. For now, the team is basically David handling both roles, Rachel who I haven't really worked with yet, and me. It's a smaller group than before. I'm hoping they fill the permanent team lead spot soon so David can go back to focusing on his Senior Technical Lead work full-time.

That does sound like a lean setup — just you, David in his dual capacity, and Rachel who's still ramping up. I can understand wanting David to get back to his core Senior Technical Lead focus so the sub-group has dedicated leadership. In the meantime, if you want me to help draft any notes to management about team capacity or resource needs, I can structure those for you. And whenever you're ready to put together that integration platform reference document, just let me know and we'll get it started.

I was looking at the internal org chart tool today and it still shows David's title as just Technical Lead — no 'Senior' prefix. I think the system is just outdated. I know for a fact his official title has always been Senior Technical Lead since I started working with him. Those tools are never up to date around here.

Yeah, internal org chart tools are notorious for lagging behind actual titles. Based on everything you've told me, David Keane's official title is Senior Technical Lead, and he's currently also serving as interim team lead for your sub-group. I'd trust your direct knowledge over an outdated system entry. If you ever need to flag the discrepancy to HR or IT so they update the tool, I can help you draft that request. Is there anything else off about the org chart?

Funny you mention HR — I also noticed the chart lists someone named Kevin Dahl as Senior Technical Lead on a completely different team, the infrastructure team. Different person, different team entirely. Anyway, I wasn't looking at the chart for fun. I was trying to figure out what's happening with the permanent team lead search for our sub-group.

Ah, so Kevin Dahl holds the same Senior Technical Lead title but on the infrastructure team — totally separate from David's role on the product integration team. And it sounds like you're eager to get clarity on when your sub-group will have a dedicated permanent team lead so David can step back from the interim duty. Have you heard any updates on the search timeline, or is it still up in the air? I can help you draft a follow-up inquiry to Tom Aldridge if that would be useful.

Actually, something came up about that today. HR told David they're planning to make the interim team lead role permanent and drop the Senior Technical Lead part, so he'd just be Team Lead going forward. David mentioned it to me after lunch. It hasn't been finalized yet though — it's still going through approvals and headcount review.

That's an interesting development. So the proposal from HR is to convert David's role entirely to Team Lead, removing the Senior Technical Lead title. Since it's still pending approvals and headcount review, nothing is official yet, but it's worth keeping an eye on. If that goes through, it would be a meaningful shift in David's responsibilities and title. Would you like me to note this as a pending change, or would you rather wait until it's confirmed before we update anything formally?

Hold off on treating that as final. David confirmed in standup that the permanent change isn't happening yet, so for now he's still Senior Technical Lead plus the interim team lead duty. He said the approvals got pushed back and there's no timeline. So his current title situation hasn't actually changed from what we discussed before.

Understood — I'll keep David's current status as Senior Technical Lead with the additional interim team lead responsibility, exactly as it's been. The HR proposal to make him just Team Lead is on hold with no clear timeline, so it's not actionable right now. If and when that changes, just let me know and I'll update accordingly. In the meantime, if you need to reference David in any emails or documents, I'll use Senior Technical Lead as his primary title and note the interim team lead duty as a temporary addition.
